utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Today because we are starting at 10.00, we will sit up to 17 hours to catch up on the last half hour. Any other counsel who wishes to examine the witness before re-examination by Mr. Pantelic? I see none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Re-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, a question from the Prosecutor relating to the political situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina after multiparty elections in 1990, you spoke about party relations, so could you please tell us: Do you know who formed the coalition government after the multiparty elections in 1992, at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina? We're talking about parties now which parties formed the government?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the government was formed by the Party of Democratic Action, the Serbian Democratic Party, and the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the principle of that coalition alliance was in some way applied at the local level as well? I'm talking about the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same principle was applied at the local level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the period up to 1991, was the principle of equality of the constitutive peoples in force?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how this worked in practice at the local level, according to what you know, and how were these interests protected, if you know? I'm thinking about the decision-making process and also the parliamentary life at the local level.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the multiparty elections in 1990, there were no particular protection mechanisms. I already mentioned in the municipality of Gradacac, since the Serbs were a minority there, the decisions were made by outvoting to the disadvantage of the Serbs. I'm talking about some decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at the local level, the government was formed between -- amongst the SDS, the Party of Democratic Action, and the HDZ. So what is your knowledge about how this functioned there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the political measures taken by the Serb delegates in this sense? How did the Serb deputies react to attempts at outvoting, this occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I didn't ask any questions relating to the functioning of the local municipality or local government after the elections. This just doesn't arise out of cross-examination. It's not relevant to the proceedings at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think since this is a last question in this topic, I think it's relevant because this witness can clarify how the system, political system, functioned on the republican level and on the local level and what the consequences of certain actions of the coalition partners were, simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are back to the same problem. It may be relevant, but the matter wasn't raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then I can go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tanasic, could you please tell me, since the Prosecutor yesterday asked you questions relating to the party organisational structure of the SDS party: Do you have any knowledge about how the SDA party was organised in Bosnia and Herzegovina? And I'm thinking about the relationships there and I'm also thinking about the functional aspects of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm objecting, Your Honour, before the witness answers. I didn't ask about the functioning of the SDA. I asked this witness about the functioning of the SDS, of which he was the local president. Completely outside the bounds of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, I mean, the coalition partners, SDS, SDA, and HDZ, I would just like to find out what are the system of organisation and functioning, just to make a parallel. And I don't see any particular problem not to explore this matter with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. With the explanation, then you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question was that if you have any personal knowledge, can you explain how the SDA party was functionally organised in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the local level, the Party of Democratic Action also had a municipal board, and at the republican level, they had a Main Board and the party presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what the situation was with the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very similar. They also had at the local level municipal boards, and at the top the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any knowledge about how many members were there in the Main Board of the SDS, if you remember, could you please tell us the numbers.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was over 80 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell me: In the decision-making process, when a decision was adopted by the Main Board, can you explain to us what its force was? Was it binding on the other party bodies or, if you know and if you can make a parallel, if the decision about implementing party policies was in the hands of an inner circle or something like that. Could you please explain that principle to us. Since you said that there were 80 members, could you please tell us what you know about that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All key decisions, more important decisions, decisions of a global importance, were adopted at the Main Board, and they were binding for the lower bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these decisions binding for the organs or officials at the highest level also of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They were binding on them also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members were there in the Main Board of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our municipal board, there were no representatives in the Main Board because we were a smaller municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the municipal level, did you have a body that was called the municipal board or the Main Board? You were a president of the municipal board. What were other bodies that existed there and what were they called?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the municipal level, it was called the municipal board, and it numbered about 40 members, comprised of representatives from all the villages of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the decision-making process, did that proceed by discussion and by adopting conclusions, or did you, as the president of the board, give certain indications and ideas that were to be adopted? How did that function?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the duty of the president was to conduct meetings of the municipal board and not to directly make decisions but to carry out those decisions which were crystalised through discussion and reached by voting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that was the same at the highest level, if the procedure was the same as you have just described it at the highest levels?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This principle applied to all the levels of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since a lot of time has passed since then, I'm interested if you can remember still in 1990 and 1991 which bodies existed at the republican level of the SDS party. You mentioned that -- if you remember, of course, that it was the -- the Main Board was there, the Executive Board. Do you remember who was the president of the Main Board of the SDS at the republican level, or of the Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was no president of the Main Board. There was a president of the party, and that was Dr. Radovan Karadzic. And as far as I can remember, there was no Executive Board, but there was a party presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what your personal knowledge is in the period of 1992 and 1993 about possible discriminatory moves and acts of Dr. Blagoje Simic in Samac? Did you hear of anything like that? And please explain to us whether you have any knowledge about that at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the question. I didn't ask the witness about discriminatory acts by Dr. Simic. I asked him only the hypothetical question in relation to the character conclusion the witness had drawn. My learned friend Mr. Pantelic asked the same question in examination-in-chief. This just doesn't arise out of anything I asked, with respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it was a little bit more expanded by my learned friend during his examination, cross-examination, because on my question with regard to the character of Dr. Blagoje Simic, my learned friend expanded that to the issues of discriminatory actions and some issues with regard to the indictment. So I'd just like to clarify that with the witness, because that was the matter which was raised by the Prosecution during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I will allow the question, Mr. Pantelic. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tanasic, do you have any personal knowledge in the period of 1991, April 1992, until the end of 1993, about discriminatory acts of Blagoje Simic relating to non-Serb ethnic groups and generally?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about any such actions by Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody -- any of the people around you or anybody from that area possibly speak about acts of such nature by Dr. Blagoje Simic? Did you hear anybody complain about his conduct or any of his acts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN TANASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about anything like that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have another question relating to the -- to a topic that was mentioned during cross-examination. Do you have any personal knowledge that in the territory of the municipality of Samac, from April 1992 until July 1992, about the functioning of the Crisis Staff? Do you have any information about that? Was there any talk about that? This was after the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this. The witness answered this in cross-examination in the clearest possible way, saying the Crisis Staff was never established. He didn't know anything about it. There is nothing that can be clarified from that answer, in my respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My impression, Your Honour, was that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- this witness was confused or to some extent misled by the questions of the Prosecution, so I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. There is no such thing as being misled. The question was quite clear and it was even further clarified by the witness

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean in terms of whether the question was focused on a period prior to the outbreak of hostilities in the municipality or after, in that term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You remember that point was also discussed yesterday, that there was no relationship as to the answer from the witness covered the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Tanasic, could you please tell me what your knowledge is about certain failings by the police in Samac? Do you have any information about certain things committed by the police in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again I object, Your Honour. I didn't -- I can't recall asking anything in relation to the police in Samac yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, in broader term, Your Honour -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are back to the same problem. It's not an opportunity for you to continue examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I think that I've finished with the re-examination of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I just want one matter with the witness. I wanted to find out: Yesterday you did say that soon after the outbreak of the war about April 1992, you went off to fight. You were a soldier. I just want clarification on that. What did you mean exactly? Were you away on the front line so that you never participated with the civilian institutions during the -- from the outbreak up to the end of 1993, or which period did you go away as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't somewhere else. I was in Pelagicevo, as part of the military unit. I was in communications in the 3rd Detachment, which means that since at that time in Pelagicevo, the municipality that was founded, and that was banned, I didn't take part in its work then or later. I was simply a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions arising from that answer? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now free. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may during this few seconds to inform the Trial Chamber that due to certain important personal commitments, I would like to -- I informed my learned friend from the Prosecution with regard to the line-up of the witnesses for today. It was scheduled to have witness Dr. Stanimirovic this morning after this witness, but I was informed by the witness unit yesterday afternoon and also by Mr. Paleksic, a witness who should come here, that he should be at latest on Monday, next Monday, in Belgrade. So I just want to inform that instead of Dr. Stanimirovic, if it's convenient with the Trial Chamber to have Mr. Paleksic as the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go ahead. Whichever witness is available, as long as the Prosecution is informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution is informed just before -- just prior to coming into court this morning. It does present us with a little bit of difficulty in that no one has prepared for the cross-examination of this next witness, because until 2 minutes to 10.00, we were under the impression that another witness was coming. So the only difficulty is we may ask for a slight adjournment after hearing his evidence in chief, because we have been taken by surprise, because the witness list keeps changing from the Defence perspective and we can't keep up with this rate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But I think this is a common problem in most trials all the time, even with the Prosecution we had these problems. I expect counsel to be prepared for cross-examination for all the witnesses listed, regardless of the sequence, please, so that we go ahead with the Defence. Can we have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In this case for instance, the Prosecution I want to pay attention. We have a list of viva voce witnesses and they're fairly few, so that it shouldn't be much of a problem to prepare for. Be ready for any to be called, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only difficulty with this one is Mr. Di Fazio was going to take this witness and he's not actually in court today. But we can -- we'll just switch it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Re. Good morning. Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, please. Examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me and can you hear the translation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you receiving proper translation when you address the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you be so kind to state your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: My name is Slavko and last name Paleksic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few remarks concerning our communication. After my question, since both of us speak the same language, you should make a slight pause in order to allow for the interpreters to translate what has been said and the transcript is properly done. And I hope that will not present a problem. Tell me: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of June, 1953, in Gracanica, in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married? Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm married, with two boys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Were your parents and your grandparents also from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, all my relatives come from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us approximately how many generations it goes back?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think that my family has been living in Bosnia around 200 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paleksic, what kind of education do you have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the faculty of law in 1977. Then I passed the bar exam in 1981 [as interpreted]. I completed my military service in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the accuracy of the transcript. The witness said that he passed his bar examination in 1979, not in 1981.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will rectify that. I will clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was: When did you take the bar exam?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In May 1977 -- 1979, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which branch of the army did you serve in?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Infantry and sub-branch president Tito's guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any rank in the military?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any, but after that I acquired the rank of a sergeant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that after you completed your military service you found a job. Where was your first employment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I got a job before I went to the army. As soon as I graduated from the faculty, I got a job in the basic court as an intern in Gracanica, and after I had taken my bar exam, I worked as a judge of the basic court in Gracanica. I also worked as a public Prosecutor of the basic court. Then I was a manager of a company. And after that, I was the secretary of the municipal assembly. That was before the war broke out, until the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We shall go back to this period. After the war broke out, you left the territory of Gracanica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left my place of living on the 29th of April, where I had been living for the previous 15 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning your further professional career, after you had left Gracanica, what did you do professionally, and in which period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: From 1st of May 1992 I had a work obligation in the police station of Petrovo, where my parents lived and where I went as a displaced person, and there I worked as chief of the legal affairs section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly: What kind of jobs did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: This is the issuing of identity cards, driving licences, passports, and various other certificates within the framework of the Ministry of the Interior Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remained there how long?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Until August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: After that I worked at the security centre service -- services centre in Doboj, as head of the section for personnel and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I presume that was a similar job.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, a similar kind of job, only at the regional level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We shall also go back to this period later. When you said "at the regional level," which particular region was covered by the Doboj regional centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior was set up in such a manner that it had several centres. The Doboj centre covered the region of Brod, Derventa, Doboj, Samac, Petrovo, and Teslic municipalities, Pelagicevo as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paleksic, can you tell me, when you were the head of the legal affairs section, that was from August 1992 until when?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Until 1st of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: After that I have to correct myself, I was an acting chief of the Security Services Centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you discharge this duty?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Until the 1st of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After April 1995, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: After that I moved to Bijeljina, where the seat of the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska was, and there I took the position of the head of the personnel and legal affairs department. It was basically the same job but only at the level of the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Until end of August 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After August 1997, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In August 1997, there was a division in the Ministry of the Interior and the leadership of Republika Srpska. I was the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska until February 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After February 1998, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: For a short while I also worked as the chief of the legal affairs section, and then, in June 1998, I opened my own law firm, and at the moment I work as an attorney at law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is your law office?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work on any cases in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I was a legal assistant in this case, prosecutor against the accused Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paleksic, are you a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No. I have never been one, or rather, I was a member of the League of Communists until 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Paleksic: What was the situation in April 1992 in Gracanica, and what was the reason for your leaving Gracanica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I was very much politically engaged as member of the League of Communists in Gracanica and I discharged various duties, like, for example, the vice-president of the municipality, president of the social political council of the municipality. The situation was similar to other towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina: Very tense, strong tensions could be felt. Gracanica was a town where both the area of the municipality and the town itself was populated by 80 per cent of Muslims, now Bosniaks, and some 15 per cent Serbs, and the rest were made up for the remaining percentage. I know that because I was at the time the secretary of the municipality when the elections were held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: What specifically happened in April 1992, after which time you left Gracanica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I worked as the assistant for morale in the Territorial Defence staff, and I noticed that the people from the town, my Muslim neighbours, were very often away, that they wore uniforms, that very often they returned with muddy uniforms and boots. And I asked one of my neighbours, who was on that staff where I was an assistant, and he was hierarchically below me, asked him where they had been going, and he replied that they were going to a military exercise. It was very indicative to me that they had been holding a military exercise and I, as his superior, did not know anything about it. I heard that weapons had been distributed and that there were some unofficial formations that were preparing themselves for war. Since I wasn't a member of any party, I couldn't believe that that could happen in Gracanica, where I had very good relations with my neighbours, despite the war that had broken out elsewhere. However, on the 28th of April, in the evening, a friend approached me - in fact, he came to my door, at midnight, to the door of my flat. He was a Romany, a gypsy. And I had helped him to bury his two sons who had been killed during a military exercise. We were very close. He was about 60 years of age at the time. And he told me -- they used to address me as "judge." He told me: "Judge, they're going to kill you tonight." I asked him, "Who do you mean?" And he replied, "You don't want to know." I took my wife and my children, and in sneakers and in shorts, left my flat and my town and I never went back. The following day, if you allow me to finish, the following day, somebody called me by phone to tell me that my flat had been plundered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you leave with your family?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I went to my parents' house in Petrovo, on Mount Ozren, which is about 20 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: For the sake of clarity, could the witness tell us the geographical location of Gracanica, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: That's very good, then. We're thinking alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paleksic, in respect to the town of Doboj, where is Gracanica located, and where Petrovo was, where you went?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Gracanica is halfway between the towns of Tuzla and Doboj. On the one side is Gracanica, and that is the side where mainly Muslim villages were situated. That is the right-hand side of the Spreca River. And on the left-hand side of the river is Petrovo, composed of Serbian-populated villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was it from Doboj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: There is about 20 kilometres between Doboj and Gracanica, and some 40 kilometres to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which direction from Doboj geographically is Gracanica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Geographically, it is exactly on the east from Doboj, to the east from Doboj. Yes, that is north-eastern Bosnia. And Gracanica is about approximately 50 kilometres from Samac. So that was the region. And it has almost the identical number of inhabitants and it is structured in the same way. These are generally small Bosnian towns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were secretary of the Gracanica municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: How long were you in this position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: All the dates that I took jobs were either the 1st of April or the 1st of October. So from 1st of October 1987 until the 1990 multiparty elections, when practically I was expelled from this job because I didn't favour any political option.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which political parties in the aftermath of the 1990 elections practically took power?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Practically, SDS and SDA, in conformity with the number of populations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the fact that you held this office and that you knew how the municipality worked, can you tell us: In the decision-making process, the municipal level, in the Municipal Assembly, which principle prevailed? How the debates were held and on what principles the decisions were based, and what was the role of the president of the municipality? Can you just be brief? Because you know that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I know very well how the municipality operated, because I was also the vice-president of the municipality. Decisions were adopted at sessions, at the proposal of the executive committee. The president was the first among equals, and his role was the role of a speaker, and he also chaired the sessions. The decisions were adopted by majority vote, and the vote of the president was equal to the vote of any of the deputies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Paleksic: Do you know -- can you just tell us briefly, do you know anything about the events in the region of Posavina in the period 1991, which means late 1991, until April 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I just heard stories about that and read about it, because at the time I was living in Gracanica. But as an official of the Security Services Centre in Doboj, and especially as the head of the section, in 1994 I learned detailed information about what had taken place in Posavina, particularly in the village of Sijekovac, Brod municipality, then in Derventa, and Novi Grad and Odzak. Because then, as an authorised official, I signed criminal charges for this Honourable Court against a number of persons who had at the time, according to these criminal charges, presumably had committed serious crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we clarify which court, which Honourable Court this is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure Mr. Pantelic will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is also my intention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paleksic, could you please just give us a few details. First and foremost, which are the persons against which you brought criminal charges, as part of the team that was involved in this Prosecution, and what were the circumstances? Could you give us a few details?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: We brought criminal charges - perhaps there was a misinterpretation - through the committee for cooperation with The Hague Tribunal from Belgrade, and we submitted this to this office of the Prosecutor, that is to say, the Office of the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal against a certain number of persons who were mostly ethnic Croats, but some were ethnic Muslims as well, for crimes committed in the camp of Novi Grad, Sijekovac, and Brod. I don't know what happened with this charge sheet, but I know that there were a lot of documents there, a lot of photographs, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you describe the atmosphere, based on what you know yourself, starting from April 1991 onwards, in political terms, I mean? I would like to know whether you have any personal knowledge as to what was going on in the republican parliament in 1991. Of course, we are talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: We all followed that very carefully, because I knew that the lives of my children and of my entire family were at stake. As Yugoslavia disintegrated - I think there's no reason for me to repeat all of this - a similar situation occurred in Bosnia-Herzegovina. There was a spillover and there was outvoting. The Croat and then Muslim people did that, and practically an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina was proclaimed. I don't want to go into the reasons why somebody felt threatened in Yugoslavia and why some other people felt threatened in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but tensions were such that at an incredible speed there was rallying along ethnic lines on all sides. It was only a question of time, in terms of days, when conflicts would break out. The conflicts started very soon, and that proved to be true, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the place where you lived, how could you describe that period, say from the end of April -- from the end of 1991 until the moment when you left? Could you give us your assessment concerning the atmosphere in the briefest possible terms?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Well, you know what the atmosphere was like in towns that have predominantly one population. You cannot really feel a pending conflict because the minority sort of withdraws and wonders what will happen. Also, the majority population lives relatively safely, so that's what the situation was like. So I belonged to a people that practically on the eve of the conflicts that were imminent just sat there and waited to see what would happen. That was the cruel truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Paleksic: In a political sense - of course, if you know, it's not all that significant, but in order to paint a complete picture - what was the situation like in a political sense among the parties in the place where you lived? Could you give us an assessment in that respect?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you what I know. Power was divided between the SDA and the SDS. Very few Croats lived there, so they did not have a party of their own. So power was divided, and everybody was tugging the rope in their own direction. However, the population that was bigger had bigger chances. There was not a true relationship of partnership. There was not a real coalition. And excuses were made to the effect that this was a struggle for toppling the previous regime, but it was obvious that it could not function normally for very long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Since you held certain positions, certain offices, during your career, how come you were not a member of the SDS? Wasn't that a prerequisite for carrying out the duties that you did?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I had the fortune or misfortune to always come to certain positions when times were uncertain or difficult. I always came to these positions on the basis of professional experience and knowledge. Nobody ever asked me to be a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In that period, say from April 1992 and further on, while you were in these state agencies, was that a prerequisite for having these jobs? Was it possible for a person who was not a member of the ruling party to get a job? Could you tell us about your personal knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Wherever I was, I gave people jobs on the basis of their professional qualifications. In leading positions, in top jobs, usually there weren't any people who were not affiliated with the political party concerned. I had the fortune or misfortune, as I said of holding certain positions in spite of the fact that I was not a member of any political party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: While you were doing your work obligation at the public security station in Petrovo, as you said, from April 1992 onwards, how could you briefly describe your work there? First of all, can you tell us what work obligation is and how did you get orders to be engaged in this way? Could you just tell us in a few words?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence, I think it was called the department, the relevant department, on the basis of professional qualifications and the education they had, allocated people to certain work obligations. I spent a few days in the army, and then they transferred me to the public security station. This was practically an order issued by the Ministry of Defence. There was a war going on and there were some places, some work places, for which very few people were qualified and then persons who actually were qualified were appointed to those jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was the period in Petrovo. And now tell me: In which capacity were you transferred to Doboj, to the regional centre? Was this also a type of work obligation or was there another procedure involved now within the ministry that you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think that two matters need to be clarified here. Work obligation is one thing, and employment is another thing. At the same time, I had work obligation which I was carrying out upon orders from the Ministry of Defence, and at the same time I was employed, and I had a decision on my employment on the basis of which my years of service were registered and I received a salary, and I also had social and health insurance, et cetera. So that's what the situation was like, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Could you explain how the Ministry of the Interior was organised, the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska? First tell us when it was established.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: It was first established at the beginning of 1992. I think it was February or March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the basis for doing that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The law and the government, and on the basis of that law, there was a law on ministries, and in this law all ministries were enumerated, their province of work, their responsibilities, et cetera. The Ministry of the Interior was established and it functioned in two parts. One was the public security section and the other one was the state security section. The public security section in which I worked functioned on the basis of departments that were organised within the republic, so there was a department of the police, department for crime prevention, department for legal affairs, a department for border matters, and I think there was a department for financial matters. And territorially, the ministry was organised on the basis of centres of public security for certain districts or regions, and within the centres there were public security stations, usually for the area of one municipality. All organisational entities had such -- had the same kind of segments that the ministry did. That is to say that the police was there, then the personnel department, general affairs, financial affairs, et cetera. The ministry functioned on the basis of the principle of subordination, and also there was a compulsory quality in its work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go into detail a bit. If you were in this regional centre, you explained a little while ago that within that regional centre there were a few public security stations that were usually in various towns; right? Now tell me: Who was superior to the regional centre? How did this function?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: It was the minister who was the superior of the regional centre, and it was the head of the centre who was the superior of public security stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour. I was informed that there are some -- yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paleksic, tell me: How was funding provided for the payroll of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: From the budget of the republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we are going down to the regional centre level. Who provided for the payroll there? Tell me, if money is allocated from the budget to the ministry, and then how is the further allocation done?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: To all the employees and in all the centres. That is to say, of course, the overheads have to be taken into account and various other expenses like for oil, accommodation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I said -- when you said "centre," then you say what?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Then the centre makes this allocation to the various stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In Doboj, you were head of the department --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I was head of the department for personnel and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that entail? What did you do, actually?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The department for personnel and legal affairs prepared for the ministry decisions related to employment; then it supervised the issuing of passports, personal identity cards, drivers' licences, traffic licences, and various decisions in that field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Paleksic: During your career at the regional centre in Doboj, did you have any professional contacts with your colleagues from the public security centre in Samac, and if so, could you describe with who and what the nature of your professional relationship was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: As head of this department, I had contacts first and foremost with the people who were engaged in these matters at the public security station in Samac from August 1992 onwards. I had contacts with the then head there, Stevan Todorovic, and the chief over there as well, Savo Cancarevic. Often they would come to Doboj for meetings, and sometimes we, as a team from the centre, would go to Samac as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Tell me now: What is the extent of these contacts, professionally speaking? What type of work was involved, from the domain of work of the Ministry of the Interior, what was it that you actually covered, and in which context did you communicate with the persons at the public security station in Samac? Could you give us a bit more detail?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: IDs were given by the Ministry of the Interior to the centres, and then we, when necessary, sent them further on to the public security stations. We wrote or dispatched instructions for the issuance of IDs. That means the procedure involved in issuing passports, drivers' licences, personal IDs, et cetera. We were also in charge of disciplinary proceedings, and we carried out certain inspections along the lines of our professional work, either on a regular basis or when necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that we've touched upon that subject, could you tell us whether in this period in 1992 there were any -- there were any checks in the public security station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In December 1992, the minister established a commission consisting of professionals from various fields, and he issued an order to check on the work of the public security station in Samac in the field of police work, the crime prevention service, and the legal service. I was the appointed member of the commission for checking on the work of the legal service in the public security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period that you are talking about, can you recall who was the member of the -- the minister for internal affairs in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think it was Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how was this technical commission founded? How were you informed about it? Can you give us details?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The communication in the ministry for internal affairs were pretty firm, and I think that the committee was formed on the basis of an order. There was a certain number of people from the headquarters of the ministry for internal affairs. I was there, and there was another colleague also from the public security centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members did this commission have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which sectors did the committee monitor, in accordance with the order of the Ministry for Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I said in my previous sentence that this was the police work sector, so relating to uniformed police, criminal activities, and the sector of public identification, so ID papers and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify a little bit here for the transcript: Could you please give us brief descriptions of these sectors? What is their area of activity and what is under their jurisdiction, like you said, because of the translation it's a little imprecise. So can we clarify that, please? Not because of any fault of the interpreters but because of the specific topic that we are talking about professionally here. So in order to have clarification.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: A police station functioned within the centre for public security. So these are police affairs, police activities, like anywhere in the world, which implies people in uniform who work out in the field. They monitor traffic, take care about public peace and order. They secure certain facilities, certain buildings. And the criminal police dealt with the processing of information for criminal charges, future investigations, and those people worked in civilian clothes. Legal affairs meant mostly the issuing of public documents for the needs of the citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, so as part of the commission there were people, members, who covered certain segments of that work and that structure. So if you remember, could you please tell me: Who were these colleagues, and which one of them was in charge of what? It was a long time ago, but --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I remember. There was Mr. Goran Saric. He was in charge of the police aspect. And there was Ostoja Minic, who was in charge of the criminal aspect. Minic, not Mijic, but Minic. Mico C Novakovic. Mico C Novakovic, for the aspect of the police, as part of the public security centre. I was in charge of legal affairs. And there was somebody who was in charge of the financial aspect, but I don't remember the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the order issued by the minister for internal affairs, when did this commission that was formed begin its work, and what was the procedure of the work of that commission whose member you were?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: It was an urgent order. I remember that. And we went to Samac right away. And everybody worked along their line of duty. Since it said in the order what were all the things that needed to be controlled, I remember that it was said that traffic and drivers' licences were being issued there without the appropriate basic documents to clarify. For example, there is no contract on the sale and purchase of a vehicle, and a traffic licence would be issued in such a case, or there is no other proof of ownership and the traffic licence would still be issued, or there was no proof of a past driver's test, and in such a case a driver's licence would be issued. While I was checking all of these things, I found that, yes, it was really so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these failings, and what was the extent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In the traffic area, I think there were over 100, but as far as the drivers' licences, I don't remember. But as far as vehicle registration, there were over 100 such cases where there was no proof of ownership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether, in your area of work, you personally came up against some other shortcomings, maybe regarding some other documents or IDs or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: There was quite a mess regarding the employment papers of some police officers and other members of staff, so it took a long time to correct all of that. There were major problems relating to drivers' licences, because they were issued without any proof of a driver's test. And I noted all of that in a separate part of the report. And I remember that I suggested to the minister that immediately over the local media, the radio stations and local newspapers, all those who received their documents in this way should be called to report in within a certain time period to correct these documents, and if they failed to do so, their documents would be declared invalid and their vehicles would be confiscated. And this is the way it functioned. And I think the minister accepted this and issued instructions to this effect, and I think that's what happened, because many people later did bring in the required documents, or some people fled, escaped, with their vehicles, or they were confiscated by the police. So this is the situation concerning my area of activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned people who ran away with their vehicles, if you remember, of course, are you talking about local citizens here or are you talking about some other people? In which context did you mention this detail?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think that they were both local people and people who had come from other places, but I don't know the proportion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to functional jurisdiction and responsibility in the public security station, who was responsible for the work of the station? I'm talking about the Samac station.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The chief was responsible, so that would mean Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what were the findings of the other members of the commission that was doing this work?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mostly in conversations I understood that there were a lot of things that were not quite right in the work of the station. In the report they were all noted down, but there were a lot of things that were not functioning properly, and the view was that the station was not being managed in a professional manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Paleksic, could you please tell me: This first check, how long did it last? What was the method of work that the commission employed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: We stayed there for three or four days. The first day, as is proper, we reported to Chief Todorovic, and then after that, Mr. Blagoje Simic was the only one who greeted us, in his office. In the commission, we knew that the minister did not form a commission purely on his own initiative. Someone from the municipality requested the forming of the commission, but I don't know who. After we completed our work, Mr. Simic held a joint dinner - I don't know what I would call it in those conditions - but I remember that he thanked me personally for coming, and he asked that order be imposed through the ministry of internal affairs. I think that I saw Mr. Simic only once before that, and I had seen Mr. Todorovic several times at meetings. I would like to say that the minister, based on our report, issued a series of orders to correct matters, and it is very interesting that he appointed an experienced commander from the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, whose name is Mirko Blazanovic. I think that at that time he had already been working for 20 years in the service. And he had instructions to oversee the work of the Samac station, Mr. Todorovic, for the next three months, and to help him in his work. So to monitor the work of the station and to help Mr. Todorovic in his work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you for a minute, Mr. Paleksic. When you mentioned this detail that Dr. Blagoje Simic thanked you for your work, and because you had come, for the work of the commission, not just you personally, what conclusion do you draw from that, or what was your impression? What were you able to conclude, based on certain facts that you were a witness to? What is your conclusion here?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Since I've known Mr. Simic, and this is my personal view --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm specifically interested in this.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: He was always very responsible, pedantic. He even overdid it somewhat. My view, my opinion at the time, was that it was important to him for everything to function in accordance to law and to regulations. And I haven't changed that opinion. I still think that that is what he wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, since you mentioned a little earlier on, even though you don't know any details, that you had heard, you had some information that somebody from the municipal government called in or asked for the formation of this commission: Did you discuss this issue with Dr. Simic in any detail about what was specifically happening in the Samac public security station regarding this and what were the repercussions and how did this reflect upon the atmosphere in the town and in the institutions? If you have any details about that.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I told Mr. Simic at that dinner what our findings were and what the suggestions were, what the proposals were, and as far as I can recall, he agreed with that, and he was satisfied to have all those things that were not functioning properly corrected. But I don't remember any other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that perhaps be clarified, whether it's in relation to the findings about the drivers' licences or other things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I talked about traffic and drivers' licences and different certificates and things, so I only discussed those things that related to my area of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to clarify the following, though: During that contact, did Dr. Simic express interest in the overall work of the commission, how that was proceeding and what were the efforts invested and the position, or is it that he was exclusively interested in your domain of work?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: He talked with all of us from the commission, Mr. Simic, and the conversation that he had with me pertained to this topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you were present at this dinner, do you recall whether other members of the commission that had come and that had completed its work had also informed the municipal leadership of Samac about their findings and about their work?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was practically the least important person there, because the findings about the legality of the police work and the criminal department were much more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I'm -- maybe I'm wrong. Is it time for our break now? Because it's one hour and 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall take our break now and continue proceedings at 12.00. In the afternoon, we shall have a break at 1550 and continue at 1610, up to 1700 hours. So we shall have one break in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paleksic, before the break, we spoke about this dinner that you had with the municipal authorities and members of the commission. You mentioned, and it's only logical, that in your job you first and immediately contacted Mr. Todorovic, the chief of the station, upon your arrival. Can you tell me, or rather, describe, what was his reaction when the ministry's commission started its investigation and when it instructed for certain documents to be reviewed and generally to do their work, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I must say that Mr. Todorovic did not receive this without a certain degree of nervousness. In addition, as far as I can remember, he graduated from a technical faculty, and so he wasn't qualified for that, and he was rather nervous. Of course, he was polite, but it was obvious that he was anxious to see us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he in any way comment on the presence of this commission and the initiative that was launched by the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Not in my presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that part of the investigation covered review of personal files, employment decisions, and other personnel issues. Do you remember if you did review these personal files of Mr. Todorovic, can you tell us when and by whom was he appointed chief of the station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, because I had seen his personal file many times later, there was some problems concerning his appointment. In fact, he was appointed in early 1992 - I don't know exactly the date - by the minister of the interior, but I know that in 1992, that took place, and after our investigation, we issued new decisions to all personnel, including Mr. Todorovic, dated -- in 1993, but the decisions were dated based on the original decisions made by the Minister of Defence [as interpreted] for the simple reason for those people to have a continuation in their service and the payment of social security, health insurance, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is I think a need for one correction in the transcript. It's page 35, line 20. Instead of the word "Minister of Defence," this witness said it was minister of interior, or minister of police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Paleksic: So the appointment letter and appointment was done by whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: It was exclusively under the jurisdiction of the minister of the interior, for all members of the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the commission completed its work, when was the final report on the findings made, and to whom was it forwarded, and what happened with it later and what was the procedure?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: According to the rules under which governing the operation of the Ministry of the Interior, the report is done immediately. So upon our return to Samac, I think we prepared the report within 24 hours. One copy was given to the chief of the Security Services Centre, and another copy was sent to the minister of the interior personally. After that, he, based on the report, prepared a series of orders pertaining to various fields in order to rectify these flaws detected in the station in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned the chief of the centre, were you referring to the regional centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Doboj regional centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what specific measures were taken by the Ministry of the Interior in that period after you had filed your report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I know specifically which measures were taken within the field that I was in charge of, so we have set up valid and good records of ID cards, drivers' licence, traffic licence, passports. We remedied the flaws where it was possible in all files pertaining to these public documents. One of the measures was to appoint a kind of revisor or supervisor who will monitor the work of the station and its chief, and I remember that one of the measures pertained to the conduct of policemen in compliance with the law on the interior and which implied the method how they were going to treat the citizens, how the dress code, how the orders were to be executed, et cetera. I don't know anything about other measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the appointment, or rather, an order on appointing a supervisor by the minister of the interior. That was Mr. Blazanovic. And you mentioned that he started to do his job. Are you aware -- do you know how long he discharged these duties, how much was he involved in supervising the public security station in Samac and what his conclusions were? Tell me just briefly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think that he stayed there about three months, which means that the problems were rather serious, since he stayed that long. His duty was to correct the method of operation and to issue instructions and guidelines for further work. I think that was fruitful because following that the public security station started to operate in a more -- in a better way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that following the work of the commission, certain problems persisted with Mr. Stevan Todorovic within the ministry and within his office. Can you offer more details about that? What was that all about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Since I was chief of the legal department of the Ministry of the Interior, and before that in the public services centre, on two or three occasions - I cannot recall exactly - Mr. Todorovic was either suspended or appointed to another post due to his non-compliance with the rules of operation that were valid in the Ministry of the Interior. I think that that became very prominent in 1995. I was present while Mr. Todorovic talked with the deputy minister, and the reasons for his transfer and suspension were always his hardheadedness and his need to do many things contrary to the rules and regulations and standard practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the fact that you mentioned that the principle how the Ministry of the Interior operated, I mean the principle of subordination, did Mr. Todorovic acknowledge the orders and instructions that he received from higher bodies within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Sometimes he did, sometimes he didn't. He wasn't the type to recognise authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how eventually - of course, if you know - this story ended with his office and engagement in the police?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: He was dismissed, but I don't know on what grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us, if you know, of course, about the cases when certain authorised services or the minister himself passed certain decisions, were these decisions put into practice concerning Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Most often the execution of these decisions relating to the status of Mr. Todorovic within the Ministry of the Interior always proved to be complicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sense?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: In the sense that he never voluntarily accepted that. He always thought that he had been demoted and degraded, that his conduct was proper. So whenever a decision was taken, he always filed complaints, which was followed by lengthy discussions, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he use exclusively official channels in this procedure or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about any other methods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Samac as a member of the commission in December 1992, what do you know about the existence of certain number of people in detention? Did you establish that fact in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: We were in the municipal building. We visited the heating plant, where I think that Mr. Simic was president. We also visited two buildings used by the security station, which is the police station and the department store, and at the time we didn't find any detainees there. To tell the truth, we didn't look for any detainees, because that was not contained in the order given by the minister. So to repeat, we did not see any detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it ever mentioned that there were people, large number of people, detained in Samac in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say a large number, I mean several hundreds.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No. This issue had never been raised, nor did I hear anything about it. Later on, in this case I heard that there were some people in detention and that they were transferred to a small town or village near Bijeljina, but at the time there was no mention of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In the period, although you started to work in August 1992 in the Doboj centre, but between April and December 1992, when you came to -- went to Samac as member of the commission, did you, in the regional centre in Doboj, have information that there was a number of detainees in Samac and that there was some illegal proceedings or crimes committed in the period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: Perhaps somebody else had. I didn't. I was mainly -- I was exclusively involved in legal issues. I first visited Samac during the war, in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a judge, now you're a lawyer, and you were involved in legal matters, tell me: What was the procedure during police interviews under the then valid rules and regulations? Was it possible and allowed at the time for a counsel to be present during this questioning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No. Only since last year in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or rather, Republika Srpska, it was allowed to have counsel present during questioning. That was not the case before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Who was authorised to conduct certain procedures, investigating procedures, and instituting criminal proceedings between April 1992 until, let's say, until the end of 1993, if a crime was committed, if there was a suspicion of crime? Can you explain to us how this was reflected, given there was a war at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: There were civilian courts and civilian prosecutor's offices. Members of the Ministry of the Interior did the on-site investigation of all forms of crimes and provided a perpetrator was a serviceman or member of the military, then the case was transferred to the military prosecutor's office, and if he was a civilian, it was transferred to the basic prosecutor's office. Criminal charges were filed by the police or citizens' charges could have been filed as well, and also the military prosecutor, but I'm not very versatile in military matters. So we had civilian prosecutors' offices and courts, and military prosecutor offices and courts, and pre-investigation procedure was mainly carried by members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were in Samac in December 1992, do you have any knowledge regarding some court proceedings that took place before the military court in Banja Luka related to some things that happened in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I familiarised myself with these cases the first time when I was a legal assistant in the proceedings here against Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that time you did not have any knowledge about these proceedings being instituted before the Court in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No. No, I had no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge regarding the fact that Todorovic, through official channels, reported to the top staff in the centre in Doboj about the detainees that were in the -- under the police station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know about that. I'm not sure that he really did report about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the prevalent practice in police work in terms of this hierarchy? The lower authority, that is to say the head of the police station, was he duty-bound to report to higher authorities about all the aspects of his work, including the number of detainees, the number of charge sheets filed, et cetera? Could you tell us what the obligation was of this lowest rank of organisation, that is to say, police stations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: The police in any state organised in the following way: That lower police stations report to higher instances on every particular matter, starting with minor occurrences all the way up to serious crimes. Reports are sent at 00 hours for the previous day every morning -- every night, and in the morning, this is on the table of the public security station, centre station, and also the minister's table. So the minister had information as to everything that happened in the republic, the head of the regional centre had information about everything that happened in the region, whereas the head of the public security station had everything within his jurisdiction. So it was the duty of the police station to report every day to the centre about things that happened on the previous day in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: You are aware of the operation related to the corridor break through in 1992. Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I can say what my experience was. Perhaps it doesn't really pertain to this case. I have a handicapped child, and this child has been under medication since birth. And this child cannot live without this medication. So now I'm telling you of my personal history. When the corridor was broken through, my child had medicine only for 21 more days. So I believe that it was necessary to establish this corridor. Whether some rules were violated in that respect, I really do not know, but I know that this was a necessity for that part of Republika Srpska where I lived. I also know of some babies who died in Banja Luka because they did not receive proper treatment. I was not in the military. I don't know how this action took place. But this is my personal experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think it was July 1992, June or July 1992. No, July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Do you have any personal knowledge about the work of the police authorities -- or rather, before that, let me ask you something else. Do you know, in the territory of the municipality of Odzak, after the corridor was established, do you know what the situation was like from an administrative point of view?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. Could Mr. Pantelic speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: There is one thing that I remember, that the public security station had complained to me that no one could enter Odzak and I asked what was this all about and he said military administration. I didn't know what military administration meant but I knew that the minister of the interior for a long time did not have the situation in Odzak under their own control. Afterwards we established a public security station there, but a few months had gone by in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we talked previously about the procedure within the ministry itself, can you tell us whether in practice, and also on the basis of law, was it possible for the Municipal Assembly to dismiss the chief of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
utterances.text: No. No. No. The chief of SUP could be replaced only by the minister of the interior at the proposal of his immediate superior, namely the head of the regional centre of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether the municipal War Presidency could replace the chief of SUP?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO PALEKSIC
